evidence: change-product-status.dto.ts: ChangeProductStatusDto.status has @IsIn(['ACTIVE', 'INACTIVE', 'DELETED']), a hardcoded copy of the ProductStatus enum's members.

change-product-status.command-handler.ts: execute() checks the same set again with ProductStatus.fromNameIgnoreCase<ProductStatus>(status) and throws InvalidFormatException built from ProductStatus.getAll<ProductStatus>().map(c => c.name).
Case-sensitivity mismatch: DTO @IsIn is case-sensitive while the handler's fromNameIgnoreCase is not, so the two checks of the same rule already disagree.

The DTO doc comment justifies the duplication as avoiding 'a 500 from deep inside the aggregate', but the handler now throws a descriptive InvalidFormatException itself, so that reason no longer holds.
change-product-status.service.ts and change-product-status.command.ts are cohesive: the service builds ChangeProductStatusCommand(productId, dto) and sends it through CommandBus.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module has one cohesive concern: changing a product's status. The service builds a ChangeProductStatusCommand from the DTO and sends it on the CommandBus. The handler loads the aggregate, calls ChangeStatus, checks broken rules, saves and publishes. That part fits the module's design.

The problem is that the set of valid status values is defined in two places that already disagree. The domain enum ProductStatus owns that set, and the handler uses it to resolve and reject values. The DTO separately hardcodes the literal list ['ACTIVE', 'INACTIVE', 'DELETED'] in @IsIn. The two checks behave differently:
- The DTO's @IsIn is case-sensitive.
- The handler's ProductStatus.fromNameIgnoreCase is not.

So the same input can be judged differently depending on which check it reaches. If a status is added to or removed from ProductStatus, the DTO literal will silently drift.

The DTO comment calls the duplication deliberate, to get a 400 that names the accepted values instead of a 500. That reason no longer holds: the handler now throws InvalidFormatException listing ProductStatus.getAll() names. Also, @IsIn could take its list from ProductStatus.getAll(), which would keep the 400 behaviour while keeping the list in one place.

This is the rubric's "duplicate a rule or invariant that should live in one place", so the unit fails. Confidence is moderate because the duplication is documented and intentional.

violations.message: ChangeProductStatusDto.status hardcodes @IsIn(['ACTIVE', 'INACTIVE', 'DELETED']), copying the closed set that ProductStatus owns. The handler checks the same set again with case-insensitive matching through ProductStatus.fromNameIgnoreCase, so the two checks of one rule already differ and the literal will drift when the enum changes. Take the list from ProductStatus.getAll() instead.
